A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same REFINE research work, with 16 readable pages including Appendices A–D. Text and rendered-page comparisons support a complete comparison; pages 3–16 are visually identical.

before.justification: v4 reports original benchmark evaluations in Tables 1–2, efficiency measurements in Figure 2, and feedback-component ablations in Table 3.

after.justification: v5 retains the original benchmark evaluations, efficiency measurements, and ablation results in Tables 1–3 and Figure 2.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Appendix B retain the same structured feedback generation, filtering, Error-book construction, and single-nearest-neighbor inference procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same MME-RealWorld reasoning, MMStar reasoning, and SEED-Bench-2-Plus tasks and subdomains, with the same dataset coverage in Section 4.1 and Appendix A.

E2.justification: Tables 1–2 retain Standard Prompting, CoT, Direct Feedback, and RICP as comparators for the same models and benchmarks. No comparator is added or removed.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 retains the same student and teacher models, temperature 0.0, pass@1 evaluation, and dataset splits. Appendix A sample counts and Section 4.3 ablation settings are also unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 4.3 and Table 3 retain the same self-regulatory, cluster-level, and CoT feedback ablations. Appendix D preserves the same illustrated error-correction example.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is unchanged. Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests for the experiments.

E6.justification: Tables 1–4, Figure 2, and the qualitative example retain identical results. For example, Table 1 reports the same REFINE overall accuracies of 41.92% for Pixtral-12B and 32.12% for Qwen2.5-VL-3B-Instruct.

T1.justification: The Error-book definition, cosine-similarity retrieval expression, and enhanced-prompt formulation in Equations 1–3 are unchanged. Neither version adds formal assumptions, theorems, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about structured feedback, multimodal reasoning, retrieval efficiency, token savings, and scalability.

C2.justification: Sections 4.2–4.3 retain the same interpretations concerning feedback specificity, model capacity, and interference from additional feedback. The limitations concerning teacher quality, error diversity, knowledge synthesis, and new domains are identical.

D1.justification: Implementation and reproducibility information remains unchanged, including the evaluation toolkit, embedding model, experimental settings, Appendix B pseudocode, and Appendix C prompts. The added author-role note supplies no new technical or resource-access information.

R1.justification: Section 2 and the references retain the same cited works and positioning relative to retrieval, multimodal reasoning, and error-driven learning approaches.

P1.justification: v5 adds a dagger to Bumsoo Kim's name and the footnote 'Corresponding author.' The arXiv version/date stamp changes, but the body wording, terminology, and section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The additional author footnote causes limited column and paragraph reflow across pages 1–2. Figures, tables, equations, and appendix displays are unchanged; rendered pages 3–16 are identical.

improvement.justification: v5 clarifies the corresponding author's role and slightly reflows the opening pages. The scientific content, evidence, explanations, limitations, and reproducibility information remain unchanged throughout the main text and appendices, establishing no meaningful overall quality difference.
